title: Secret Key Leakage Across Next.js Server-Client Boundary
businessContext: A fintech startup operates a subscription billing portal built with Next.js App Router. A security vulnerability report flags that the live production JavaScript bundle downloaded by customers in their browser contains `sk_live_...` Stripe Secret API keys in plain text.
problemStatement: A Server Component page fetched tenant payment settings and passed the entire database configuration object as a prop into a Client Component `<PaymentSettingsForm />` decorated with `"use client"`. Even though the form only displayed the currency and public key, Next.js serialized the entire prop object into the client HTML payload (`self.__next_f.push(...)`), exposing the live private secret key.
constraints: Stripe secret keys must never be bundled or serialized into client HTML/JS payloads.
Only public publishable keys (`pk_live_...`) may be exposed to the browser.
Use package `server-only` to guarantee build-time enforcement against server module importation into client code.
candidateTasks: Explain how Next.js App Router serializes props passed from Server Components to Client Components.
Refactor the page to sanitize props and only pass explicitly allowed public fields: `{ publishableKey, currency }`.
Explain how `import "server-only"` works at build time to prevent accidental secret leakage.
hints: Props passed to "use client" components are serialized into JSON within the RSC flight payload embedded in HTML.
Never pass raw database models or config objects directly across the client boundary; project or DTO-sanitize them first.

testCases.name: Prevents secret key serialization across RSC boundary
testCases.explanation: Enforces strict data transfer object projection.

alternativeApproaches: Using Server Actions for sensitive operations so secrets never touch the client at all.
Using experimental taint API: `experimental_taintUniqueValue` or `experimental_taintObjectReference` in React/Next.js.
commonMistakes: Thinking "use client" components run only in the browser and cannot access server data: they receive whatever props the server passes to them.
Naming secret environment variables with NEXT_PUBLIC_, which automatically bakes them into client JS bundles.
